[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

In federated delivery models, many contributors can modify prompts, schemas, and agent behavior simultaneously. Uncontrolled changes cause regressions, policy drift, and broken audit trails.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Route all changes to AI agents through a governance gateway with tiered approvals: classify change type and risk, apply the approval matrix for that type, require validation and rollback evidence, and record the approved change metadata before deployment.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- For all Production AI agents — the gateway applies to every change regardless of perceived impact
- When multiple domain teams are making changes to a shared or referenced agent configuration
- When rollback capability must be documented before a Production change is deployed
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Every Production change is traceable to a change record with approval evidence
- Rollback paths are established before problems occur
- Change type classification exposes high-risk changes that would otherwise be treated as routine
page_texts.9:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The federated model grants domain teams the authority to modify their agents' prompts, configurations, and schemas. This autonomy is valuable but creates governance exposure: without a change gateway, a single team's change can affect the user experience for an entire workflow domain, and there is no mechanism to detect or reverse changes that cause quality regressions or policy violations.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Configured agents on M365 Copilot can be modified directly in the Agent Builder interface without a separate change record. Custom agents are modified via code changes. In both cases, the platform does not enforce a change review process — governance of the change process is an organizational responsibility.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without a change gateway:
- Prompt changes that affect output schema or policy compliance may be made at any time by anyone with edit access to the agent configuration
- There is no record of what changed between versions, making regression investigation slow and often inconclusive
- Rollback paths are undocumented — when a change causes a regression, the rollback must be improvised under incident pressure
- Change authority is undefined — teams may not know who needs to approve what type of change
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Domain teams need to move quickly; adding approvals adds latency
- The change gateway must be lightweight for low-impact changes and rigorous for high-impact changes — a uniform approval requirement for all change types would create unsustainable overhead
- Rollback readiness documentation is low-cost relative to the risk of an undocumented rollback under incident pressure
page_texts.14:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Route all changes through a governance gateway that implements a tiered approval matrix based on change type. The gateway has four components:

1. **Classify change type and risk** — every change is classified per the change type taxonomy in STD-GOV-AI-004 before the approval path is determined. Change type classification is the most important step: it routes the change to the correct approval tier.

2. **Apply the approval matrix by change type** — the approval matrix in STD-GOV-AI-004 assigns the required approvals for each change type. Metadata changes require only domain owner approval. Policy and governance changes require Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval. Classification determines the path.

3. **Require validation and rollback evidence** — all Production-bound changes must include a reference to the validation plan (per STD-TEC-AI-005) and a documented rollback plan. Rollback readiness must be confirmed before deployment.

4. **Record approved change metadata** — after approval, the change is recorded in the capability change log with all required change record fields per STD-GOV-AI-004. The deployment does not proceed without the change record.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Proposed Change] --> B[Classify Change Type\nper STD-GOV-AI-004]
    B --> C{Approval Tier}
    C -- "Metadata / Ownership /\nLifecycle State" --> D[Domain Owner]
    C -- Prompt Wording --> E[Domain Owner +\nPlatform Governance\nValidation Lead]
    C -- "Intent Scope / Output Schema /\nSystem Connection Register" --> F[Domain Owner +\nPlatform Governance\nReview]
    C -- "Policy / Governance" --> G[Platform Governance +\nEnterprise Architecture\nBoard]
    C -- "Lifecycle Promotion" --> LP[Quality Gate Sign-off\nHigh-Tech Governance Review]
    D & E & F & G & LP --> H[Document Change Record\n7 Required Fields]
    H --> I[Execute Validation Plan\nvs Scenario Suite]
    I --> J[Confirm Rollback\nReadiness]
    J --> K[Deploy + Append\nDeployment Result]
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Change type classification | Determines the approval tier required for the change | STD-GOV-AI-004 |
| Approval matrix | Defines required approvals per change type | STD-GOV-AI-004 |
| Change record | Documents the change, rationale, risk, and approval evidence | STD-GOV-AI-004 |
| Validation plan | Defines how the change will be tested before deployment | STD-TEC-AI-005 |
| Rollback plan | Documents how the change will be reversed if it causes regression | STD-GOV-AI-004 |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Contributor proposes a change to a Production agent
2. Contributor classifies the change type using the taxonomy in STD-GOV-AI-004
3. The classification determines the required approvals from the approval matrix
4. Contributor documents the change record (7 required fields per STD-GOV-AI-004), validation plan, and rollback plan
5. The approval path is followed — required approvers review and approve or reject
6. On approval, the change is validated against the scenario suite before deployment
7. The deployment is made and the change record is finalized by appending the deployment result and timestamp — approval evidence must already be recorded in the change record before deployment, per the approval matrix
page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Emergency path**: for compliance incidents or critical defects, expedited approval with domain owner minimum approval, immediate Platform Governance Team notification, and post-change review within the defined window
- **Batch change path**: related changes are batched into a single release under a single change record, reducing audit surface and regression risk compared to deploying individually
page_texts.20:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Change type taxonomy and approval matrix documented in domain governance documentation (per STD-GOV-AI-004)
- Change record template accessible to all domain contributors
- Emergency change criteria defined before any emergency arises
- All domain owners and governance reviewers trained on the approval matrix
page_texts.22:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#phase-1-change-gateway-establishment]

#### Phase 1: Change Gateway Establishment

1. Document the change type taxonomy and approval matrix per STD-GOV-AI-004 in the domain's governance documentation
2. Define the emergency change criteria (what constitutes an emergency, what triggers expedited approval)
3. Define the change backlog channel and triage cadence for the domain
page_texts.23:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#phase-2-active-change-governance]

#### Phase 2: Active Change Governance

1. For every proposed change: classify the change type, determine the approval path, open a change record
2. Complete the rollback plan before beginning the change
3. Execute the validation plan after the change and before deployment
4. Confirm rollback readiness before deploying to Production
5. Append the deployment result to the change record after deployment (approval evidence must already be recorded before deployment, per the approval matrix)
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#phase-3-change-quality-audit]

#### Phase 3: Change Quality Audit

1. Monthly: verify that all Production changes in the prior month have complete change records and followed the correct approval path
2. Quarterly: assess whether the change type classification taxonomy and approval matrix are correctly calibrated — are high-impact changes being classified correctly?
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Classify the change type before any work begins — classification after the fact is vulnerable to rationalization bias
- Document the rollback plan before making the change — rollback planning under incident pressure produces inadequate plans
- Batch related changes into a single release to reduce deployment events and the corresponding regression risk
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- Classifying higher-impact changes at a lower tier to avoid the required approval — particularly, classifying behavioral or schema changes as "wording changes"
- Skipping the rollback plan for changes perceived as low-risk — the rollback plan is required for all Production changes regardless of perceived risk
- Conducting the validation plan after deployment rather than before — validating in Production reverses the gate

page_texts.29:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- 100% of Production changes must have complete change records
- Rollback readiness must be confirmed before every Production deployment
- Change type misclassification discovered after deployment is a non-compliance event requiring incident review
page_texts.30:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

- The minimum approval for each change type is defined by the approval matrix in STD-GOV-AI-004; domain owner approval is the minimum only for change types where the matrix assigns it as the lowest tier
- Higher change tiers require Platform Governance Team and/or Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval per STD-GOV-AI-004
page_texts.31:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| Change record completeness rate | 100% | Monthly change quality audit |
| Change failure rate (changes causing regression) | Declining over time | Incident review |
| Mean time to restore after regression | Declining over time | Incident records |
| Rollback plan presence | 100% of Production changes | Change record audit |
page_texts.34:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#scenario-1-prompt-wording-change-requiring-validation]

#### Scenario 1: Prompt wording change requiring validation

A domain team proposes a wording change to an agent's prompt that does not change the output schema but alters the tone of a specific output section. The change is classified as a prompt wording change, requiring domain owner approval and Platform Governance Team validation lead review. The validation plan confirms that the regression baseline still passes. The change is deployed with a complete change record.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#scenario-2-emergency-compliance-change]

#### Scenario 2: Emergency compliance change

A compliance incident requires immediate addition of a new disclaimer to all production agents. The emergency change criteria are met. The domain owner approves under the expedited path. The Platform Governance Team is notified immediately. Rollback readiness is documented — the prior prompt version is archived. The change is deployed. A post-change review is completed within three business days.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Contributors modify agent prompts and configurations directly without change records. Regressions are discovered by users, not by the team. Rollback requires recreating the prior prompt from memory or trial-and-error.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

All Production changes have complete change records with classified change types, approval evidence, validation results, and rollback plans. Regressions are reversed from the documented rollback plan rather than reconstructed.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-012-federated-change-gateway-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Uncontrolled changes to federated AI agents cause regressions, policy drift, and broken audit trails in Production.

**Solution:** Route all Production changes through a tiered approval gateway — classify change type, apply the approval matrix, require validation and rollback evidence, and record the change before deployment.

**When to Use:** All Production AI agents; any environment where multiple contributors can modify agent configurations.

**Key Benefits:**
- Every Production change is traceable to a change record
- Rollback paths are established before incidents occur
- Change risk is proportional to the approval burden

**Implementation Complexity:** Low to Medium

**Prerequisites:** Change type taxonomy, approval matrix, change record template, emergency criteria defined

**Related Patterns:** PTN-TEC-AI-010 Shared Guardrail, PTN-GOV-AI-009 Portfolio Rationalization
